seoTitle: Transfer a Domain to GoDaddy from Any Registrar
metaDescription: Move a domain to GoDaddy from any registrar, including Namecheap. Learn how to unlock it, get the EPP/Auth code, and check for free transfer offers.
intro: Moving a domain between registrars sounds intimidating, but GoDaddy's transfer flow reduces it to unlocking the domain at its current home, grabbing one code, and pasting it into a two-step form. This guide walks through where that flow actually lives inside a GoDaddy account, what the transfer landing page tells you about pricing before you commit, and what the process looks like once a domain is queued up in your cart — including how a transfer can end up costing nothing for the first year. It works the same way regardless of which registrar you're leaving, whether that's Namecheap, Hostinger, or Bluehost.

steps.heading: Get your EPP/Auth code and unlock the domain first
steps.body: Before touching GoDaddy at all, log in to your current registrar and find the domain lock setting, usually under the domain's management page. Switching it off is what makes the domain eligible to leave. While you're there, request the EPP code (also called an Auth code) — most registrars generate this instantly under a "Transfer" or "Domain details" section, sometimes emailed to the account's registered address. Without this code, GoDaddy has no way to verify you're authorized to pull the domain over, so get it in hand before starting anything on the GoDaddy side.

steps.heading: Open Domains from your GoDaddy account menu
steps.body: Once logged into GoDaddy, click My Account in the top bar to open the dropdown, which lists Manage My Products, Shop GoDaddy.com, and a Quick Links section with Domains, Websites, Hosting & WordPress, Email & Office, and SSL Certificates. Selecting Domains from here takes you into the domain management area where transfers, DNS, and portfolio settings all live — it's the hub you'll return to throughout the process, not just the entry point.

image.caption: The My Account dropdown in GoDaddy, with Domains listed under Quick Links — the starting point for a transfer.

steps.heading: Check pricing on the Transfer your domain page
steps.body: GoDaddy's dedicated Transfer your domain page lays out the cost up front: a flat rate for popular extensions like .com, a separate discounted rate if you already own the matching country-code version (the example shown lists ₹999 for a .com and ₹749 for an already-owned .in domain), and a note that the transfer includes a free year of registration. Reading this page before you start is worth the minute — it tells you exactly what the transfer will cost and confirms your domain's extension is eligible before you go find your EPP code.

image.caption: The Transfer your domain landing page, showing per-extension pricing and the free year of registration included with a transfer.

steps.heading: Add your domain in the transfer wizard
steps.body: Clicking through starts GoDaddy's two-step transfer wizard, beginning with "Step 1 of 2: Add domains." You can type or paste up to 500 domains at once, or import a file if you're moving several. As soon as you enter a domain, GoDaddy runs a validation check against the registry to confirm it's unlocked and eligible — the tool shown here displays "Validating domains... 0 of 1 processed" while it works. If validation fails, it's almost always because the domain lock wasn't actually switched off at the old registrar, so double back to step one if that happens.

image.caption: Step 1 of GoDaddy's transfer wizard, validating a domain against the registry before it can proceed to the authorization code step.

steps.heading: Enter the EPP code and submit the transfer request
steps.body: After a domain passes validation, step two asks for its EPP/Auth code — the code you pulled from your old registrar earlier. Paste it in exactly as given; a single mistyped character is enough to reject the request. Submitting here doesn't move the domain instantly — it sends a transfer request that your current registrar has to release, which is why getting the domain unlocked in step one matters so much.

steps.heading: Review the cart and confirm the free-transfer pricing
steps.body: Before finalizing, GoDaddy shows the domain in a cart summary, confirming the transfer, the one-year term, and the price — in the example here, a .nl domain transfer showing ₹0.00 due now, with a note that it renews in July 2026 for ₹868.70. This is where the free-transfer offer becomes concrete rather than theoretical: if your extension qualifies, the transfer itself is free and you're only committing to the renewal price a year out. Check this screen carefully so you know exactly what you're paying today versus what renews later.

image.caption: The order summary confirming a domain transfer at ₹0.00, with the renewal price shown separately for the following year.

steps.heading: Track the transfer status until it completes
steps.body: After confirming, the transfer moves into a pending state that typically takes five to seven days to finish, since your old registrar has a window to approve or automatically release the domain. Check back under Domains → Transfers in your GoDaddy account for status updates, and watch for common snags — a domain still locked, a mismatched EPP code, or a domain registered too recently to be eligible for transfer. Once it clears, the domain shows up in your regular portfolio like any other GoDaddy-registered name.

faq.question: Does this process work for domains from any registrar?
faq.answer: Yes, the general steps apply broadly, including transfers from registrars like Namecheap or Hostinger, though the exact unlock and EPP code screens will look different at each registrar.

faq.question: Are all domain transfers to GoDaddy free?
faq.answer: No. Pricing depends on the extension — the transfer page shows the current rate per extension, and some transfers include a free year of registration, but that's not universal across every TLD.

faq.question: What common errors can happen during a transfer?
faq.answer: The most frequent issues are an incorrect EPP/Auth code, a domain that's still locked at the old registrar, or a domain that hasn't met the minimum registration age required before it can be transferred.

faq.question: How long does the transfer usually take?
faq.answer: Most domain transfers take around five to seven days to fully complete once initiated, since the losing registrar has a window to approve or auto-release the domain.

faq.question: What happens if the transfer wizard says my domain failed validation?
faq.answer: This almost always means the domain lock wasn't switched off at the current registrar before you started. Go back, confirm it's unlocked, and re-enter the domain in the transfer wizard.
